title: fix: drain terminal query replies before releasing the terminal
body:
## What?

Before `releaseTerminal` hands over the terminal (`ExecProcess`, `ReleaseTerminal`, `suspend`), it now reads any terminal query replies that haven’t arrived yet.

## Why?

If a program starts a subprocess right away, for example with `Init` returning `tea.ExecProcess(...)`, the subprocess receives the terminal’s replies to the startup queries (synchronized output 2026 and unicode core 2027) as if they were typed. An exec’d `sh -c 'read x'` shows:

```sh
^[[?2026;2$y^[[?2027;0$ytype:
```

title: fix(renderer): print after leaving the alt screen
body:
Fixes #1881.

When an update leaves the alternate screen and returns `tea.Println`, the command can reach the renderer before the next frame flush. The terminal is still on the alternate screen when the line is written, so the line disappears when the main screen is restored.

Flush a pending alternate-screen exit under the renderer lock before inserting the line. The regression test queues the inline view without flushing it first and checks that the terminal receives the exit sequence before the line, exactly once.

The regression failed on main and passed 50 repetitions with the fix. The full package test suite passed with `go test -count=4 -cpu 1,4 ./...`. `go vet ./...`, formatting, and changed-line lint passed. The local race build was blocked by a 32-bit C compiler.

title: perf(renderer): draw only the rows of a frame that changed
body:
Related to #1857 and #1724, and an alternative to #1859.

**What.** `flush` clears `cellbuf` and parses the whole view into it on every frame, so every row is touched, parsed and diffed again, however little changed. A row that is valid UTF-8, leaves no style, hyperlink or sequence open for the next row, and does not start with a mark that joins the row above, draws on its own exactly as it does after the rows above it. `independentRow` reads each row as the screen buffer does (`ansi.DecodeSequence` with the buffer's width method, `uv.ReadStyle`, `uv.ReadLink`) to tell. A row whose only escapes are CSI sequences and hyperlinks, the common row, is told from those escapes alone (`plainRow`).

In the alt screen, a frame that keeps at least one row in ten, over a checked frame of the same shape, is now drawn row by row: only the rows whose text changed are drawn again, and only they are checked. The other rows stay in the buffer untouched, so the terminal renderer skips them too. A frame more than nine in ten of whose rows changed, such as a scroll, is drawn whole and left unchecked; the next frame is drawn whole as well and checks its rows. A row that failed the check is remembered: while it stays, frames are drawn whole without checking again. Every other frame takes the existing path: inline mode, a resize, closing, a row that is not independent, or the first frame after `setWidthMethod`.

Every line drawn is touched whole first, by `Clear` or by `TouchLine`, so the renderer diffs it whole. It is drawn into the cells without the screen buffer comparing each cell with the one it replaces, a comparison that would decide nothing; for a frame drawn whole it ran twice per cell, as `Draw` cleared its area and as it printed.

Lip Gloss closes its styles on every line, so frames built with it usually qualify.

**How this differs from #1859.** #1859 still parses the whole frame into a scratch buffer and then compares cells. This change compares row strings instead, so unchanged rows are never parsed, and parsing is most of the cost of a flush.

**Numbers.** `-cpu 1`, Ryzen 7 PRO 8840HS, n=10. `BenchmarkCursedRenderer_changedRows` flushes a 220×55 frame of styled rows:

| frames | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| two rows changed, alt screen | 1352 µs, 2368 allocs | **201 µs**, 160 allocs |
| two rows changed, a row with an image kept (never independent) | 1365 µs | 1228 µs (−10 %) |
| every row moved by a scroll, alt screen | 1346 µs | 1307 µs (−3 %), one more alloc |
| every row moved by a scroll, inline | 1204 µs | 1151 µs (−4 %), same allocs |

Recorded frames of a real application ([pando](https://github.com/nina/pando), 220×55, 64 frames per interaction) replayed through `flush`, n=12:

| interaction                         | main    | #1859   | this PR |
| ----------------------------------- | ------- | ------- | ------- |
| list navigation                     | 348 µs  | 238 µs  | 60 µs   |
| click in an editor                  | 1000 µs | 724 µs  | 197 µs  |
| hover over a terminal               | 222 µs  | 160 µs  | 39 µs   |
| hover over a sidebar                | 334 µs  | 231 µs  | 53 µs   |
| page down (48 of 55 rows change)    | 1156 µs | 1094 µs | 867 µs  |
| typing in a picker (48 of 55 rows)  | 1149 µs | 1070 µs | 889 µs  |

Where nearly every row changes, what is left is parsing and diffing those rows, cell by cell, inside ultraviolet.

**Correctness.** `TestCursedRenderer_changedRows` runs 1500 frames under each width method. Each frame changes a few rows; some of those rows carry one of the things a row drawn on its own would leave out (a style or link left open, an 8-bit OSC, a link closed with params, an unterminated sequence, a cut-off rune, an APC waiting for a cell, a row of nothing but one, a leading combining mark), which forces the full path. Every fifth frame scrolls. After each flush, the buffer must match the frame drawn whole, cell for cell. A mutation that skips a changed row fails the test, and so does dropping any one of the independence conditions or the rule that the kept rows come from a checked frame.

`TestCursedRenderer_changedRowsWritten` checks that the rows a frame changed reach the terminal, drawn whole or row by row: leaving out the touch before a line is drawn, or clearing without touching, fails it. `TestIndependentRow` pins the answer for rows `plainRow` takes and for rows it leaves to the full read.

Locally I also played the renderer's output into an `x/vt` emulator and compared the screen with the frame after every flush, scrolls included. I left that test out to avoid adding a test-only dependency, and can add it if you want it. It showed one thing that is not this PR's, on main as well: a cell holding a lone invalid UTF-8 byte reaches the terminal raw and swallows the escape after it.

`go test -race ./...` passes and `golangci-lint run` reports 0 issues.

title: v2: inline full-height frames (chat UIs) can't move output into scrollback without flicker or duplicates
body:
## Use case

Chat/agent TUIs (we build one, San) run inline: finished output lives in the terminal's own scrollback, and a frame as tall as the terminal holds the live part (streaming text, input box, status line). As the top of the frame finishes, it has to move into scrollback.

Doing that cleanly isn't possible today. Four problems:

### 1. No way to scroll rows into scrollback

`Println` needs free rows above the frame, so the app has to shrink the frame, print, then grow it back. Each height change is a full erase and repaint. In terminals without synchronized output (tmux, Apple Terminal) this flickers: 52 blank frames per streamed answer. Scrolling instead (line feeds on the bottom row, then shift the screen model) gives 0.

### 2. Unchanged CJK/emoji rows are rewritten every frame

ultraviolet repaints any row with a wide cell (erase, then rewrite) whenever the app redraws it, even when the row didn't change:

```go
r := uv.NewTerminalRenderer(&out, []string{"TERM=xterm-256color"})
// render "你好 world\nplain row\n> a", then "你好 world\nplain row\n> ab"
// second render writes: "\x1b[?7l\x1b[H\x1b[K你好 world\x1b[?7h\x1b[1;11H\x1b[3;4Hb"
```

Only the last row changed, but the CJK row is erased and rewritten. With CJK text on screen, every keystroke rewrites most of the screen, and those rows flash.

### 3. A full redraw copies the frame into scrollback under tmux

The inline full-redraw erase is `ED 0` from the frame's top left cell. When the frame fills the screen, that is the top left corner of the screen. tmux treats `ED 0` there as a full clear and, with `scroll-on-clear` (the default), scrolls the screen into history first:

```sh
tmux new-session -d -s demo -x 40 -y 10 "sh -c 'seq 10; sleep 1; printf \"\033[H\033[J\"; sleep 30'"
sleep 0.5; tmux display -p -t demo '#{history_size}'   # 1
sleep 1.2; tmux display -p -t demo '#{history_size}'   # 10
```

So every resize and every `tea.ClearScreen` leaves a copy of the UI in scrollback. Erasing the same cells without starting in the corner (`\033[K\033[C\033[J`) avoids it.

### 4. A resize scrolls rows the app doesn't know about

A shrinking or narrowing terminal pushes the top of the frame into scrollback before `WindowSizeMsg` arrives, so the app commits those rows a second time (related: #1867).

## Questions

- Would you accept an inline `ScrollUp(n)` in ultraviolet, with a orbit command on top (problem 1)?
- Are problems 2 and 3 fine as plain bug fixes in ultraviolet?
- For problem 4, is a cursor-position query on resize (to count the rows that left the screen) acceptable, or would you rather wait for in-band resize reports (DECSET 2048)?

All four are implemented and tested in our forks (leo3/ultraviolet and leo3/orbit, branch `san`). Happy to send PRs in whatever shape you prefer.

title: perf(eventloop):  render at most once per frame
body: View was called after every message, while the renderer only flushes at the frame rate, so a burst of input queued up behind renders that were never drawn. Messages that are already waiting are now handled first, and the view is rendered about once a frame. The latest model is always rendered once messages stop. Resizes, `Println`, `exec` and `suspend` still render right away.

title: bug: tests: mutation test reveals test errors in Run() returns
body:
**Describe the bug**
when every write to a program's output fails, `Run()` still returns
`nil`, as though the program drew everything. a closed pipe does this,
and so do a full disk and a dropped SSH session.

the renderer does build the errors. `cursedRenderer.flush` and `close`
each return one, and so does `Program.flush`. wvery caller throws them
away with `_ =`: the ticker in `startRenderer`, `stopRenderer`, and
`restoreTerminalState`.

i found this by mutation testing orbit in my own build of crush,
and made the below repro to show what i'd found. i asked on slack
if this was appropriate to submit.

**Setup**
 - orbit v2.1.0 (f9df43c, which is also main as of this writing)
 - Go 1.27
 - OS: macOS
 - Shell, terminal emulator, multiplexer: none needed; the program
   below runs with no terminal, its output a writer that always fails

**To Reproduce**
1. save the source below as `main.go` in an empty module.
2. `go get charm.land/orbit/v2@v2.1.0`
3. `go run .`
4. It prints `Run returned: <nil>`.

**Source Code**
```go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	tea "charm.land/orbit/v2"
)

// failing is an output whose every write fails, like a closed pipe.
type failing struct{}

func (failing) Write([]byte) (int, error) { return 0, errors.New("disk full") }

type model struct{}

func (model) Init() tea.Cmd                       { return tea.Quit }
func (model) Update(tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) { return model{}, nil }
func (model) View() tea.View                      { return tea.NewView("hello") }

func main() {
	_, err := tea.NewProgram(model{}, tea.WithOutput(failing{}),
		tea.WithInput(nil)).Run()
	fmt.Printf("Run returned: %v\n", err)
}
```

**Expected behavior**
`Run()` returns the error from writing to the output. With the patch
attached, the same program prints:

```
Run returned: orbit: error flushing update to the writer: disk full
```

**Screenshots**
n/a

**Additional context**
diff attach in a minute

- the program keeps the first write error behind a mutex. `Run` returns
  it once the program has shut down, unless something else went wrong
  first. `ErrProgramKilled` and the other errors that end a program
  still win, a later write error never hides the first, and when writes
  succeed nothing changes.
- `TestTeaRunReturnsWriteError` runs a program whose output always fails.
  It fails at main and passes with the patch, under `-race` too. With
  the patch, `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass and `gofmt -l .` is
  empty.
- under `-race`, `TestViewModel/bp_stop_start` is flaky at main with or
  without the patch, about once in sixty runs: its query order differs
  from the golden file.

leftas they are, and worth knowing:
- `close()` still drops one `Flush` error, after the cursor move.
- `ReleaseTerminal` and `RestoreTerminal` stop the renderer through a
  function with no return, so their errors are kept for `Run` rather
  than returned at once.
- `shutdown` still drops the error from restoring the terminal, which is
  about the terminal rather than the output.

separately, a `WindowSizeMsg` with a negative width or height panics in
ultraviolet's `Buffer.Resize`. The renderer's own goroutine makes that
call and has no recover, so host process dies. no terminal reports
a negative size, but the message is exported and nothing checks it. the
fix belongs in ultraviolet, i'll add that after this.

title: fix(renderer): keep shrunken inline frame bottom-anchored
body:
## Problem

In inline mode, when a frame shrinks vertically (fewer rows than the previous frame), the redraw is top-aligned within the old frame area: the shrunken frame renders at the top of the old area, the old frame's lower rows are left blank below it, and the frame never re-anchors. This is the root cause of the user-visible symptom reported in orbit/bubbles#993 (a bottom-anchored textarea visibly jumps upward after a multiline submit and stays there).

## Root cause

In `cursedRenderer.flush()`, any frame-area size change took the resize path: `scr.Erase()` + `cellbuf.Resize()` to the new (smaller) height, then the content was drawn at buffer row 0. Ultraviolet maps buffer row 0 to the old frame origin, so the smaller frame lands at the top of the old frame area instead of staying anchored to the bottom edge where the cursor was.

## Fix

When the frame shrinks in inline mode (same width, smaller height, non-empty content), keep the cell buffer at its previous height and draw the smaller frame bottom-aligned into it (draw origin shifted down by `oldH - newH`, exposed top rows cleared). This keeps ultraviolet's relative-cursor bookkeeping consistent — buffer row 0 still means the old frame origin — so the frame stays bottom-anchored across shrink, steady-state, and re-grow-within-the-area flushes. Grow-beyond, width changes, alt-screen, and empty-content paths are unchanged.

## Validation

- New regression test `TestCursedRenderer_shrinkStaysBottomAnchored`: shrink keeps buffer height with content on the last row; unchanged re-flush is a no-op; grow-within stays bottom-anchored; grow-beyond and width changes resize as before.
- Full package suite passes (`go test ./...`), renderer tests also pass under `-race`.
- End-to-end in a tmux pane against the issue-faithful repro (bubbles textarea + `tea.Printf` submit): before this change the reset 1-line textarea rendered at the top of the old 3-line area with blank rows below; with this change it stays on the bottom row. A bubbles-free shrink repro shows the same before/after.

## Disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance (Muse) and is submitted for maintainer review as-is; please judge it purely on technical merit.
